quests.instruction: Aarav’s class has 6 rows with 5 desks in each row. To find the total number of desks, he multiplies. Later, the teacher shares 30 pencils equally among 6 tables. To find how many each table gets, she…
quests.hint: Sharing equally is the reverse of putting equal groups together.
quests.explanation: Multiplying joins equal groups into a bigger total. Dividing splits a total into equal groups. They undo each other.
quests.funFact: The × and ÷ symbols first appeared in printed math books in the 1600s.

quests.instruction: The football team came off the muddy field with filthy shirts. Their coach’s shirt, which had stayed on the sideline all afternoon, was still…
quests.hint: The coach stayed on the sideline all afternoon, away from the puddles.
quests.explanation: The coach avoided the mud, so his shirt stayed the opposite of the players’: spotless rather than filthy.
quests.funFact: Many animals, such as pigs and buffalo, roll in mud to cool down.

quests.instruction: A flagpole stands straight up, so it’s vertical. A fallen log lying flat across the path is…
quests.hint: Think of a flagpole and a fallen log: which direction is each?
quests.explanation: Vertical lines go up and down. Horizontal lines run flat from side to side, like the horizon.
quests.funFact: The word “horizontal” comes from “horizon”, the line where the sky seems to meet the ground.

quests.instruction: Ravi wears size 9 shoes. His little sister’s shoes are only size 1, because her feet are much…
quests.hint: Compare the two sizes. Which one is the lower number?
quests.explanation: Her shoe size is lower than his because her feet are smaller. The comparison flips big feet into small feet.
quests.funFact: Children’s feet grow fastest in their first years, which is why shoes need replacing so often.

quests.instruction: A burst water pipe is a major problem. A tiny scratch on the table leg is a ___ problem.
quests.hint: Think about which problem could wait until next week.
quests.explanation: Major means big and important. Minor means small and not very serious.
quests.funFact: In music, major scales often sound bright and minor scales often sound more serious or sad.

quests.instruction: The lift sign says “Maximum: 8 people”, meaning the most it can carry. The word for the smallest amount needed or allowed is…
quests.hint: Maximum is the most allowed. What word is its mirror image?
quests.explanation: Maximum is the most; minimum is the least. Signs use both to set the limits of what’s allowed.
quests.funFact: Some highways show a maximum speed and a minimum speed.

quests.instruction: Priya used to take ten minutes to type one email. After weeks of practice, it takes only two. Her typing has become…
quests.hint: What happened to the time it takes?
quests.explanation: Taking less time means speeding up. Her slow typing has turned into faster typing.
quests.funFact: Typewriters became popular in the 1870s.

quests.instruction: A single candle lit the table. After the power cut, Dad brought ___ candles to light the whole room.
quests.hint: One candle lights a table. How many do you need for a whole room?
quests.explanation: Single means just one. Multiple means more than one.
quests.funFact: People have used candles for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Sita’s cinema seat is close to the screen, so the picture looks huge. Her brother sits at the very back, so his picture looks small because he’s sitting…
quests.hint: Things look smaller the farther away you are.
quests.explanation: The same screen looks bigger when you’re near it and smaller when you’re far from it.
quests.funFact: Artists use the fact that far-away things look smaller to make flat drawings look three-dimensional.

quests.instruction: Maya lined up her marbles from smallest to biggest, which is ascending order. Then she reversed them, from biggest to smallest, which is ___ order.
quests.hint: Which way does the list go when the sizes shrink?
quests.explanation: Ascending means going up in steps. Descending means going down in steps.
quests.funFact: Planes “descend” when they come down to land.

quests.instruction: “How much for this kite?” “Fifty rupees.” The first speaker wants to buy it. The second is ready to…
quests.hint: One person has the kite, the other has the money.
quests.explanation: One person pays and receives the kite, the other gives it away and receives the money.
quests.funFact: The word “bargain” can mean something sold for less than its usual price.

quests.instruction: Of the planets on the school poster, Mercury is the nearest to the Sun. The planet at the other end of the poster, Neptune, is the ___ from the Sun.
quests.hint: Mercury is at one end of the line; look at the other end.
quests.explanation: Nearest means the shortest distance. Farthest means the longest distance.
quests.funFact: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to go around the Sun once.

quests.instruction: Everyone in class 5B passed the quiz. In class 5C, the quiz was so hard that ___ got full marks.
quests.hint: If everyone didn’t get full marks, how many did?
quests.explanation: “Everyone” means every person. “No one” means not a single person.
quests.funFact: “Everyone” and “no one” both take a singular verb: “everyone is”, “no one is”.

quests.instruction: The wind that bent the big palm tree was strong. By evening, it had faded to a ___ breeze that barely moved the leaves.
quests.hint: Compare the wind that bent the palm tree with the evening breeze.
quests.explanation: A strong wind has plenty of force; a weak one hardly has any.
quests.funFact: Sailors use the Beaufort scale to describe wind from calm to hurricane force.

quests.instruction: Two rival village teams decided to join forces and unite for cleaning day. When the work was finished, they…
quests.hint: Think about what happens to a team after the job is done.
quests.explanation: To unite is to come together as one. To split up is to separate into different groups.
quests.funFact: The United Nations was founded in 1945 to bring countries together.

quests.instruction: At the start of the year, the spelling list had short words like “cat”. By June it had longer ones like “necessary”. The words had become more…
quests.hint: Which list would make you pause and think?
quests.explanation: Short words are easier to spell than long, tricky ones. As the words grew harder, spelling got more difficult.
quests.funFact: English spelling has odd rules, such as “ough” sounding different in “through” and “though”.

quests.instruction: The sunflowers bloomed in July. After weeks without water in the August heat, the flowers began to…
quests.hint: Picture sunflowers in the August heat with no water.
quests.explanation: To bloom is to open into flower. To wilt is to droop and lose freshness.
quests.funFact: Plants wilt when their cells lose water and can’t hold the leaves up.

quests.instruction: Grandma mended the hole in Raj’s sleeve. If he catches it on the fence again, he might ___ it.
quests.hint: Think about cloth that is snagged on a fence and pulled hard.
quests.explanation: To mend is to repair something. To tear is to rip it open.
quests.funFact: Patchwork quilts were traditionally made from leftover scraps of cloth.

quests.instruction: Walking from the sunny courtyard into the cinema, Leo couldn’t see a thing until his eyes adjusted. The cinema was much ___ than outside.
quests.hint: Why did he have to wait for his eyes to adjust?
quests.explanation: Moving from full sun to a cinema means moving from lots of light to little. The room was darker than outside.
quests.funFact: Your pupils grow larger in dim light to let more light in.

quests.instruction: Dad polished the old copper pot until it gleamed. Using a rough scrubber would only ___ it.
quests.hint: Think about what a rough scrubber does to a mirror-like surface.
quests.explanation: To polish is to rub a surface until it shines. To scratch is to leave marks on it.
quests.funFact: Copper turns green over time, like the Statue of Liberty, because it reacts with air and moisture.

quests.instruction: The puppy in the garden is only three months old. Next to the ancient tortoise beside it, which has lived for decades, the puppy seems very…
quests.hint: A three-month-old puppy next to a tortoise that has lived for decades.
quests.explanation: Three months is the beginning of life, while decades is a long time. The puppy is young; the tortoise is old.
quests.funFact: A puppy’s baby teeth start falling out at around four months old.

quests.instruction: Putting leftover rice in the fridge helps keep it fresh. Leaving it on the counter all night in summer can make it…
quests.hint: What happens to food that stays warm for too long?
quests.explanation: Keeping food fresh stops it going bad. If it’s left out in the heat, it can spoil.
quests.funFact: Fridges slow down the growth of bacteria that make food go bad.

quests.instruction: Fireworks should only be handled by trained adults. A child lighting one alone would be doing something…
quests.hint: Think of the choice that could lead to burns.
quests.explanation: Safe activities keep you from harm. Lighting fireworks alone isn’t safe: it’s dangerous.
quests.funFact: Some places ban fireworks near forests because sparks can start fires.

quests.instruction: Making toast takes two steps, which is simple. Building a model robot from 300 tiny parts is…
quests.hint: Building a robot from 300 parts is the job that needs the instruction booklet.
quests.explanation: Simple means easy to understand or do. Complicated means it has many parts or steps.
quests.funFact: Many complicated machines are built from lots of simple parts working together.

quests.instruction: The nurse walked quietly through the ward at night. Most patients were in bed with their eyes closed, but one was sitting up reading, still…
quests.hint: Which patient had the light on?
quests.explanation: Having closed eyes and resting means asleep. The reader, sitting up with a book, was awake.
quests.funFact: Many hospitals dim their lights at night to help patients sleep.

quests.instruction: In Mr. Rao’s class, homework is due at the exact minute, with no exceptions: very strict. In Ms. Das’s class, a day’s extension is fine, so she is more…
quests.hint: One teacher accepts late homework; the other doesn’t.
quests.explanation: Strict means firmly following the rules. Lenient means going easy on them.
quests.funFact: “Lenient” comes from a Latin word meaning “soft” or “mild”.

quests.instruction: Everyone in the country knows the cricketer’s face. He’s famous. The boy who cleans the pitch every morning is mostly…
quests.hint: Think of someone whose face strangers would spot in the street.
quests.explanation: Famous people are known by many. Unknown people go unnoticed, even if they do important work.
quests.funFact: “Famous” comes from a Latin word related to “fame” and “talk”.

quests.instruction: A laptop can be carried from room to room, so it’s portable. A built-in kitchen oven can’t be moved. It’s…
quests.hint: Which one could you take along on a train?
quests.explanation: Portable things can be moved easily. Fixed things stay where they were put.
quests.funFact: The first portable transistor radios appeared in the 1950s.

quests.instruction: In the chess club, new players who’ve just learned the moves are beginners. The man who has won the city championship five times is an…
quests.hint: Think of someone who has won the city championship five times.
quests.explanation: A beginner is just starting. An expert has lots of skill and experience.
quests.funFact: Experts in any skill usually have years of practice behind them.

quests.instruction: At the quiz, the host asked, “Which animal has a long trunk?” Dev put up his hand to…
quests.hint: After the host asks a question, the contestant has a job to do.
quests.explanation: The host asks and the player answers. Those two roles complete each other.
quests.funFact: Nobody is sure where the word “quiz” came from.
